sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Open Code Review is an AI code review command-line tool from Alibaba. It reads your git diff, sends the changed files to an LLM agent that can search the codebase, and returns structured review comments pinned to exact lines.
sixtySeconds.problem: General-purpose coding agents used for review often skip files on large changes, report issues at the wrong line, and vary in quality with small prompt changes. Open Code Review adds deterministic steps for file selection, bundling, rule matching and comment positioning around the agent.
whoFor: Developers who want AI review before opening a PR
Teams adding automated review to CI
Claude Code, Codex or Cursor users who want a review skill
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a review tool that came from Alibaba's internal reviewer, with line-level comments and a benchmark showing higher precision than a general agent at about a ninth of the tokens.
requirements: An LLM provider, unless you use delegation mode

overview: You can use it as a CLI (ocr) or as Agent Skills in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Kimi Code and similar agents. Native mode uses Open Code Review's own model configuration; delegation mode lets your current coding agent do the review with its existing model and login, following the tool's pipeline.

Configure a provider with ocr config provider and ocr config model, which test connectivity. Then run ocr review in a repository to review staged, unstaged and untracked changes, or pass --from and --to to review a branch or range.
The README's benchmark (AACR-Bench: 50 repositories, 200 real PRs, 10 languages) reports higher precision and F1 than Claude Code with the same model, though lower recall. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.

troubleshooting.solution: Configure a model with ocr config provider and ocr config model, or use delegation mode.
Native mode uses Open Code Review's own provider settings, not your Claude subscription.
